correctness.rationale: For each smooth parameter, the genus is six by a complete branch-point Riemann–Hurwitz argument. A full six-element regular differential basis is established by valuations. Cartier coefficient extraction yields an explicit 6x6 symbolic matrix over F5[lambda], with fifth-root semilinearity correctly handled. Two complete semilinear chains prove the rank lists for lambda=0 and lambda nonzero over an algebraic closure. An independent polynomial expansion certificate and full F25 test confirm both cases, including nontrivial Frobenius twists. No finite experiment is mistaken for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns all smooth parameters in a fixed non-diagonal degree-seven Kummer deformation, locating an a-number jump and different entire Cartier nilpotence profiles inside one constant-zero-p-rank family. The closest Fermat-type p-rank and BT_1 theorems cover the undeformed case, not the family-wide perturbation; broader and equivalent formulations were examined. No covering table or theorem emerged from primary full-text comparisons, targeted searches, the accessible research record, or the ten local preceding claims. Residual unindexed literature risk is explicit, and independent priority certification is not asserted.
residual_risks: An older genus-six cyclic-trigonal Cartier computation may use a different normalization of the lambda*x deformation and remain unindexed.

value.rationale: The finding describes an entire natural smooth deformation stratum of cyclic genus-six trigonal covers, not an arbitrary finite sample. All Jacobians have p-rank zero yet the a-number jumps sharply 2 to 4 and nilpotence-chain lengths change 5 to 3; those structures are invisible to the published p-rank formula for the starting Fermat curve. The exact singular divisor and full smooth-parameter classification make the result a useful geometric boundary for deformations of low-p-rank curves without claiming a general moduli theorem.
